title: Home Depot Stock Drops 3% Despite $43.4B Revenue Beat as Profit Outlook Disappoints
body: Key takeaways Home Depot stock drops 3% despite earnings beat Quarterly revenue climbs 4.9% to $43.4 billion Weaker profit outlook overshadows CEO succession announcement Home Depot stock ( NYSE: HD ) fell approximately 3% in early trading on November 17 despite the home improvement retailer reporting better-than-expected quarterly revenue and earnings. Investors focused instead on a disappointing full-year profit outlook and continued pressure on the US housing market. According to Home Depot's official earnings release , fiscal third-quarter sales increased 4.9% to $43.4 billion, exceeding Wall Street expectations of approximately $42.8 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $3.86 per share, narrowly beating the $3.84 consensus. The stock declined even as comparable sales grew 2.2%, suggesting investors remain concerned about how much growth the retailer can deliver while housing activity remains weak. Home Depot Earnings Beat Expectations, but Margins Slip Home Depot's net earnings increased to $3.7 billion from $3.6 billion a year earlier, while reported diluted EPS climbed to $3.72 from $3.62. However, stronger sales did not translate into equally strong profitability. The company's adjusted operating margin declined to 13% from 13.3% a year earlier. Customer activity also showed signs of weakness. Comparable transactions fell 0.5%, while the average comparable transaction value increased 3%, indicating that higher spending per visit helped offset fewer purchases. The average ticket reached $93.09, compared with $90.39 last year. These figures highlight the uneven consumer environment previously reflected in weakening housing demand . Profit Guidance Weighs on Home Depot Stock The retailer narrowed its fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings outlook to approximately 2% growth from the previous range of 0% to 4%. That implies adjusted earnings of roughly $14.98 per share, slightly below analyst expectations of approximately $15.05. Management expects total sales to increase about 4.5% for the year, with comparable sales rising 1.4%. Its full-year adjusted operating margin is projected at approximately 12.8%. The cautious profitability outlook comes as elevated mortgage rates continue discouraging home purchases and major renovation projects. Earlier housing market data also showed that lower borrowing costs have not consistently restored buyer demand. For Home Depot, fewer housing transactions can reduce spending on flooring, appliances and large remodeling projects. Home Depot Names Richard McPhail as New CEO Alongside the earnings report, Home Depot announced that Chief Financial Officer Richard McPhail will become CEO on November 23. McPhail will replace Ted Decker, who will remain chairman. Ann-Marie Campbell will become president and chief operating officer, while Jordan Broggi takes over as CFO. The leadership changes arrive during a challenging period for consumer-sensitive companies, with recent stock market weakness adding pressure across Wall Street. Higher Treasury yields and borrowing costs have also complicated the outlook for businesses tied to household spending.

title: Analyst Sends Price Trend Warning to XRP Holders
body: XRP has been sliding since its peak in mid-2025. Crypto analyst JD (@jaydee_757) has tracked the asset’s weekly chart closely, and his latest post carries a clear warning. After months of Lower Highs and Lower Lows forming inside a falling wedge, XRP’s breakout in late August produced what appeared to be a Higher High. JD dismissed it, labeling it a fake. The chart has since proven him right. XRP has continued lower. A new Lower Low has now been confirmed near $0.95, where XRP marked its lowest level in two years . JD’s post leaves little room for interpretation: “BEARS remain in CONTROL for now.” $XRP WEEKLY WARNING: DOWNTREND CONTINUATION! After a FAKE HIGHER HIGH, #XRP continues forming LOWER HIGHS and LOWER LOWS! Another LL CONFIRMED! BEARS remain in CONTROL for now… Will my PINK BOX FINALLY HIT?! pic.twitter.com/b4JRu9vjAK — JD (@jaydee_757) November 16, 2026 The Structure JD is Tracking The weekly chart tells the story with precision. From the $3.40 Higher High, XRP carved out a sequence of Lower Highs and Lower Lows across more than a year of trading. Each attempted recovery failed to exceed the previous peak. Each pullback fell further than the last, forming the falling wedge . The August rebound broke above the previous Lower High briefly, prompting some optimism. However, the follow-through never came. XRP reversed, fell back inside the channel, and printed a fresh Lower Low. The bear structure remains intact. The Pink Box Target JD has had a specific downside target on this chart for some time. He calls it his “pink box,” a demand zone sitting between roughly $0.60 and $0.75. He previously warned that failure to sustain momentum could send XRP into his box . His post reiterates that risk. XRP is already at very low levels, but the pink box represents his view that it may need to flush lower before any sustainable recovery develops. The Longer Cycle View JD’s chart extends a white vertical line out to 2028, labeled “2028 TOP?!” This sits at the far right of the chart, beyond the current price action. This suggests that XRP’s major top for this market cycle may not arrive until 2028, leaving significant time for the asset to work through its current structure before any significant upside materializes. XRP traded at $0.9514 at the time of the chart. The falling wedge continues to compress the asset’s price. The analyst references “green box targets” on the monthly chart as his eventual profit-taking zone. Those levels sit well above the current price and remain a longer-term consideration. title: US Supreme Court Turns Down Custodia Bank Appeal Over Federal Reserve Master Account
body: TL;DR The Supreme Court denied Custodia Bank’s petition on November 16, leaving a lower ruling in place. The decision is a refusal to review the case, not a full Supreme Court opinion on crypto banking. Debate over limited master-account access remains a separate regulatory question. Custodia Bank has reached the end of a significant route through the US federal courts in its effort to obtain direct access to Federal Reserve payment services. On November 16, the Supreme Court denied the Wyoming-chartered institution’s petition to review the dispute. The decision leaves a lower-court ruling in place. It is not a fresh opinion deciding every question about crypto-focused banks or an announcement that all such institutions must be kept out of the payments system. The docket states a narrow outcome Supreme Court docket 26-62 records a straightforward entry: the petition was denied on November 16, 2026. The justices did not agree to hear oral arguments and issue a merits opinion on the dispute. In practical terms, the lower-court position remains operative, but the denial should not be presented as the Supreme Court affirmatively endorsing each part of the earlier reasoning. This procedural distinction is important. It marks the end of this review attempt while leaving future policy and account-design questions to regulators, lawmakers and separate legal processes. Why Custodia sought the account A Federal Reserve master account gives a qualified institution access to central-bank payment services without depending on another bank for the same connection. Custodia applied through the Kansas City Fed in 2020, arguing that its state bank charter supported its request. The application was denied in January 2023 following disputes over the institution’s business model and the risks the Fed identified. Custodia challenged the outcome, contending that federal law limited the Fed’s discretion. The appellate ruling instead recognised discretion to approve or deny applications in the relevant circumstances. For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's crypto licensing proposals . The debate now moves toward policy design The banking system is already debating whether some new financial firms should receive narrower forms of direct payments access. A proposed limited or “skinny” account would not necessarily provide the same services or rights as a full master account. That difference matters to institutions building business models around settlement speed, access costs and interest treatment. Even if a different account structure emerges, a future limited product should not be confused with the full access Custodia originally sought. The exact eligibility conditions and supervision requirements will determine whether such designs change the industry materially. What this means for digital-asset businesses Crypto companies operating as banks or partnering with banks have a commercial interest in dependable dollar settlement, but charter status and payment-system access are not interchangeable. Firms may still use intermediary banking arrangements, with associated concentration and operational risks. The Custodia decision removes one possible path to overturn a prior denial; it does not prohibit new applications or resolve every question about emerging financial infrastructure. The next informative developments will be formal Fed rules, account approvals and the requirements attached to them. The practical consequence for businesses is continuing uncertainty rather than an abrupt change to payment access. A firm can be licensed at the state level and still face a separate federal assessment of whether it may hold a Reserve Bank account. Policymakers who want to expand access must resolve supervision, settlement risk and eligibility in rules that Reserve Banks can actually apply. Meanwhile, fintech firms may keep using correspondent banks and other intermediaries, with the associated costs and dependencies those arrangements create. For related context, see our earlier report on custody arrangements for a US bitcoin ETF . The clearest fact is in the court record: review was denied. Whether the broader US payment system opens new pathways for digital-asset banks depends on future decisions, not on an expansive reading of this one-line order. title: FED Expected to Raise Interest Rates in December! But the Rate Move Could Shake Bitcoin! According to Wintermute, the 2022 Scenario is Back on the Agenda!

The report, updated at 02:00 EST on November 17, 2026, said HYPE had dropped to a three-month low and was struggling to attract buying interest. HYPE fell 8.03% in a week despite its Upbit and Bithumb listings. title: XRP Forms a Bullish Weekly RSI Divergence as Buyers Face First Test at $1
tags: Market|Latest XRP (Ripple) News Today|XRP Price Prediction
body: XRP’s weekly RSI held above its June low as price fell below $0.90. A weekly close above $1 would strengthen the case for a recovery. XRP fell below $0.90 over the weekend, setting a lower price low even as its weekly relative strength index held above its June trough. That bullish divergence suggests the latest decline carried less downward momentum. A weekly close back above $1 would give buyers their first evidence that the improvement in momentum is translating into a price recovery. XRP traded near $0.9601 on November 17, according to CoinMarketCap, putting $1 about 4.2% above the market. Buyers have already recovered some ground since November 14, when XRP touched $0.8943. The following day, it ended the week near $0.975, still below the dollar mark. XRP Made a Lower Low While Weekly RSI Held Up The divergence developed across two selloffs several months apart. In June, XRP was still trading above $1 when its 14-week RSI dipped just below 30, the conventional oversold threshold. By November, XRP had fallen further, yet weekly RSI stood at 35.23 when the price was $0.9542. The week was still open, so that reading can change before the close. XRP registered a lower price low in November while its 14-week RSI held above its June trough. The reading of 35.23 came before the weekly close. RSI compares the size of gains and losses using weekly closing prices. One detail matters here: RSI has actually fallen since the late-summer rebound. The bullish signal comes from comparing June with November. Sellers pushed XRP to a lower price in November, but the losses recorded at weekly closes were less dominant than they had been around the June low. At 35.23, RSI also remained well below its midpoint of 50. That leaves room for selling pressure to ease while the broader downtrend continues. Why Reclaiming $1 Matters August offers a recent example of what buyers have been able to do around $1. XRP traded near $0.98 in mid-August before reaching roughly $1.70 on August 22. The November selloff erased that advance and took XRP below the level where the rebound began. For a recovery to gain credibility, buyers would first need to close a week above $1 and defend it on a pullback. That would establish support above the November low and bring the $1.10 area back into view. XRP closed near $1.11 on November 8, just one week before it finished below $1. On the downside, $0.89–$0.90 remains the immediate test. It also overlaps the daily lower Bollinger Band near $0.90 . A weekly close below the November low would weaken the reversal case and put the longer-term support area near $0.78 back in focus.

title: Solana Foundation Takes Majority Stake in CoinGecko in Major Push Into Crypto Data
tags: News|CoinGecko|coingecko trading|crypto data push|solana|Solana Foundation|solana foundation stakes
body: The Solana Foundation has acquired a majority interest in CoinGecko, one of the cryptocurrency industry’s leading market data platforms, in a move that could significantly expand Solana’s reach among crypto investors. The partnership is expected to bring new trading capabilities to CoinGecko’s website, mobile application and GeckoTerminal platform. Announced during the Breakpoint conference in London on November 17, the deal could give Solana access to CoinGecko’s 18 million registered users and the 180,000 applications and businesses that rely on its data services. Neither organization has disclosed the purchase price or the exact size of the Foundation’s reported stake. Solana Looks to Bring Trading Directly to CoinGecko Vibhu Norby, chief product officer at the Solana Foundation, revealed the majority interest, outlining plans to expand the relationship beyond market data and research. One of the central goals is to introduce Solana-powered trading across CoinGecko’s website, GeckoTerminal and mobile application. This could allow users to discover digital assets, monitor market movements and eventually execute trades without switching between different platforms. The initiative also includes plans to explore additional decentralized finance tools and broaden the range of assets available to users. However, trading remains an area under exploration rather than a confirmed feature launch. CoinGecko’s own announcement described the initiative as part of its broader expansion strategy, with further development expected across market intelligence, data infrastructure and trading capabilities. CoinGecko Plans Broader Coverage of Digital Assets The partnership is also expected to accelerate CoinGecko’s data and research services. The platform intends to expand its coverage of onchain assets, derivatives and tokenized real-world assets (RWAs), while strengthening the infrastructure supporting its data services. CoinGecko has built a substantial presence i n the crypto industry over more than a decade. The company reports having 18 million registered users and more than 50 million monthly sessions. Its APIs also support approximately 180,000 crypto applications and businesses. According to the Solana Foundation, CoinGecko provides market information covering more than 50 million cryptocurrencies across over 2,000 exchanges. Expanding this infrastructure could strengthen the platform’s position as digital asset markets become increasingly connected to traditional financial products. Broader coverage of tokenized stocks and other real-world assets could also help CoinGecko serve a wider audience of investors and financial institutions. Data Transparency Remains a Key Priority Despite the new backing, CoinGecko has emphasized that its commitment to independent market coverage and transparent data practices will remain unchanged. The company plans to continue relying on its proprietary technology and publicly accessible methodologies while investing in improvements to the quality, speed and accessibility of its information. Its website, mobile application and API will continue operating as usual, according to the announcement. The development is particularly significant given the influence that major crypto data platforms have over how investors discover assets and assess market activity. CoinGecko’s continued coverage of the wider cryptocurrency market will therefore remain important as its relationship with Solana expands. Solana’s Latest Move Expands Its Reach Across Crypto The agreement represents another step in Solana’s efforts to strengthen its position across the broader digital asset industry. Rather than focusing exclusively on blockchain infrastructure, the Foundation’s involvement with CoinGecko could create a more direct connection between discovering cryptocurrencies and participating in their markets. The move also brings comparisons with Binance’s acquisition of rival data provider CoinMarketCap in 2020, demonstrating the strategic importance of market information platforms within the crypto industry. For Solana, access to CoinGecko’s established user base and business network could create additional opportunities to attract developers, traders and investors to its ecosystem. For CoinGecko, the backing could accelerate product development while opening the door to new ways for users to interact with digital assets. The precise financial terms and ownership structure have not yet been made public, leaving some details of the agreement unanswered. title: Alibaba Stock Falls Amid New U.S. AI Chip Rules for Overseas Data Centers
body: Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA) shares fell more than 3% to $87.70 in Tuesday’s regular trading amid newly announced U.S. licensing restrictions affecting advanced American AI computing equipment used in overseas data centers serving Chinese companies. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced the measures on Monday, issuing an interim final rule scheduled to take effect upon publication in the Federal Register on November 19. The restrictions address two concerns: advanced American processors being diverted through certain countries and Chinese companies accessing U.S. computing power remotely through foreign data centers without importing the chips into China. Alibaba’s Hong Kong-listed shares also declined, closing Tuesday at HK85.45, down 5.21% after touching an intraday low of HK85.10. The company’s U.S.-listed shares fell 3.98% to $90.62 in Monday’s regular session, after declining 13.8% during the week ended November 13. Those earlier weekly losses preceded the formal BIS announcement. Alibaba’s Reported Overseas Computing Links The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Singapore-based Megaspeed provided Alibaba with Nvidia-powered computing capacity through data centers in Malaysia. The Financial Times separately identified Alibaba as a major customer of Megaspeed’s Southeast Asian cloud business. In a joint statement , the U.S. Commerce and Justice departments said Megaspeed has been under investigation since 2024 for potential export-control violations. The agencies also confirmed that Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025. A separate report documented a financial arrangement involving the companies. The Straits Times reported on November 12, in an article updated November 13, that Malaysian corporate records showed Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix, had pledged computing and network equipment, intellectual property, and related rights as security to Alibaba-owned Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) under a June 18, 2024, agreement. The records confirmed that the security arrangement remained active as of November 11, 2026. However, they do not confirm whether Alibaba still uses Megaspeed’s computing services or how much computing capacity it uses. What the New U.S. Licensing Rules Require The BIS rule sets two separate licensing requirements: one for five specified countries and another for certain data centers worldwide. Under the first requirement, exports and reexports of covered advanced-computing items to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil will require licenses. Transfers of those items within the five countries will also require authorization. BIS identified these locations as presenting elevated risks that semiconductors could be diverted to unauthorized destinations. The five-country requirement does not apply to qualifying transactions involving end users or ultimate consignees headquartered in the United States, or whose ultimate parent is U.S.-headquartered, provided the exporter, reexporter, or transferor meets the required reporting conditions. The second requirement applies worldwide to exports, reexports, and in-country transfers of covered computing items when the exporter, reexporter, or transferor knows the items are destined for a data center that provides, or will provide, more than 12 million units of aggregate total processing performance (TPP) to or for companies headquartered in China, Macau, or other restricted locations. It also covers companies whose ultimate parent is headquartered in a restricted location. TPP measures chip processing capability. Capacity supplied through linked data centers counts toward the threshold. However, this threshold does not apply to the separate licensing requirement for the five specified countries. The worldwide restriction also covers known indirect arrangements in which intermediaries train AI models for affected companies or supply those companies with trained models. An exclusion applies when computing access is used exclusively for narrowly defined commercial recommendation systems and the required information is submitted to BIS. However, this exclusion does not extend to generative AI systems or remove the separate licensing requirements for the five specified countries. Existing data centers providing computing services covered by the worldwide restriction must obtain authorization within 90 days of the rule’s effective date to continue those services or risk future export restrictions. BIS will review license applications individually. The reported relationships do not establish whether any current arrangement involving Alibaba falls under the new licensing requirements. No resulting interruption to Alibaba’s computing access or quantified financial loss has been confirmed. Alibaba’s AI Cloud Growth and Infrastructure Spending Access to computing infrastructure is particularly important for Alibaba as it expands its AI cloud business and invests in additional computing capacity. Alibaba’s AI Cloud and Compute Services generated RMB 48.44 billion ($7.14 billion) in revenue during the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up 45% from the same period a year earlier. Of that total, AI-related products contributed RMB 12.38 billion ($1.82 billion), marking their twelfth consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year revenue growth. During the same quarter, Alibaba reported capital expenditures of RMB 67.68 billion ($9.98 billion), up 75% from RMB 38.68 billion a year earlier. Alibaba said the higher spending reflected continued investment in AI infrastructure, changes in hardware procurement cycles, additional CPU computing capacity to prepare for demand for AI agents, and higher chip component prices. Alibaba is scheduled to report its September-quarter financial results before the U.S. market opens on November 19, the same day the BIS rule is scheduled to take effect. The earnings release will provide updated figures on the company’s cloud operations and infrastructure spending. title: Bitcoin Price Outlook for November: $62,000 Decides If the Six-Week Slide Ends
body: Three Things to Know Bitcoin tried to steady after a six-week losing streak, while Strategy kept buying through the slump. Momentum gauges show the coin deeply oversold, yet sellers still control the trend. The floor near $62,000 now decides whether bottom hunters are right or early. Bitcoin paused on Tuesday after a bruising week. Strategy added more coins, and Galaxy Digital said sentiment looks like past market lows. Traders now face one question. Is this a real bottom, or only a breather before sellers push the coin lower? Bottom Hunters Circle as Bitcoin Extends a Six-Week Losing Streak Bitcoin tried to steady itself on Monday, Nov 16, after a seven-day skid of roughly 13%. The drop stretched its losing streak to six weeks. Some traders now hope last week's low marked the bottom. Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, kept buying through the slump. The company said it bought 485 BTC last week for $33.4 million, about $68,887 per coin. It now holds 850,849 BTC at an average cost near $75,452. Risk-tolerant traders also have a leveraged option. The Direxion Daily Bitcoin Bull 2X ETF (BTCU), which debuted in May, aims for 200% of the daily returns of a spot bitcoin ETF. Headwinds remain heavy. A hack of a Binance hot wallet drained an estimated $6.4 billion, the largest crypto heist on record. Market chatter also links bitcoin sales to investors raising cash for the Anthropic IPO, a pattern seen before the SpaceX listing. Bulls argue leverage has been flushed out. Galaxy Digital said the fundamental case has strengthened, citing debasement risk from large deficits and 5% yields. The firm added that sentiment has swung to "blockchain, not bitcoin" for the third time. The first two swings marked lows. Bitcoin Trades Far Below the $76K Averages Strategy Paid Near Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView Bitcoin traded near $65,000 on Tuesday, little changed over the past 24 hours. The coin has lost about 20% over the past month and sits close to that stretch's lows. A quiet session after a steep fall often means sellers are catching their breath. Price still hugs the lower end of its recent range, with no higher low yet. Moving averages tell the bigger story. A moving average smooths out daily swings by tracking the average closing price over a set number of days. Both the 50-day and the 200-day averages now sit near $76,000. That overlap matters. In a healthy uptrend, the shorter 50-day line runs well above the longer 200-day line. When the two meet, the gains of recent months have been erased. Bitcoin now trades more than $10,000 below both lines, so they act as a ceiling overhead. Strategy gives the same zone extra weight. Its average cost per coin sits just under those averages, which leaves the largest corporate holder underwater. The company has shown no sign of selling. Any rally toward the averages would bring its holdings back to breakeven and test how much supply waits there. Sellers Stay in Control Despite Deeply Oversold Readings RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 24 on the daily chart. Readings below 30 count as oversold. That means selling has run far and fast. Oversold readings often come before relief bounces. Still, a low RSI is no buy signal on its own. In strong downtrends the gauge can stay pinned in oversold territory for weeks while price keeps sliding. Other signals point the same way. MACD, a tool that compares short and longer-term price trends, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings also show a real trend, and sellers lead it. Until momentum turns, any bounce looks like a pause inside the decline. Why $62K Is the Line Bulls Must Hold Support sits near $62K, the same level traders hope marked the bottom. Buyers stepped in there during the recent skid, and the daily chart shows price bouncing off that floor. Holding it keeps the bottom case alive. A close below that level would change the picture. The next support waits near $59K, and a slide there would undercut the idea that the low is in. Resistance looks far away. The first ceiling sits near $75K, just under the moving averages and close to Strategy's cost basis. Sellers who bought higher may use any rally there to exit. Reclaiming that ceiling would be the first real sign the slide has ended. A move above the next barrier near $80K would confirm it. Two Paths for the Next 72 Hours Bullish: Buyers keep defending the floor, and the stretched RSI fuels a relief bounce toward the first ceiling. A close below the floor would cancel this path. Bearish: A daily close under the floor opens the way to the next support level below. Sellers would then keep control of the trend. A recovery above the first ceiling would cancel this path. A Bounce Is Possible but Not Yet Earned Bitcoin looks stretched enough for a rebound. The trend still belongs to sellers until price reclaims the first ceiling overhead. Fallout from the Binance hack or more IPO-driven selling could crack the floor quickly. Traders holding leveraged bets would feel that drop twice as hard. title: Almost 50,000 BTC in 2 Weeks: More Pain Ahead for the Bulls?
body: The primary cryptocurrency has fallen by over 20% in the past month, but recent whale activity suggests the real bottom has yet to form. Waning institutional interest also signals more pain ahead, with several analysts warning the price could crash to multi-year lows in the short term. Whales Push the Sell Button Instead of stacking BTC at a discount, large investors apparently believe the asset is on the verge of a further collapse. According to Ali Martinez, they have sold or redistributed 48,618 coins (worth nearly $3.4 billion) in the last two weeks alone, reducing their total holdings to around 13.68 million units. Such aggressive offloading floods an already fragile market with coins and signals a clear lack of conviction among BTC’s most influential holders. Their actions may spread panic across the community, prompting smaller players to cash out as well, thus intensifying the sell-off. The whales’ distribution isn’t the only bearish element. Heavy outflows from spot BTC ETFs suggest that pension funds, hedge funds, and other risk-averse institutions have been trimming their exposure, adding another major roadblock to a sustained recovery. As CryptoPotato reported , investors pulled more than $1 billion from these investment vehicles last week. A growing number of analysts warn that Bitcoin faces an even sharper downturn ahead. X user Mookie believes that if it fails to reclaim $66,500, it could crash toward the July low of around $57,700. Whale Scan was more bearish, arguing that the asset has been perfectly mirroring the pattern from 2017 and 2021 and predicting a potential meltdown to $35,000 in the next less than two weeks. Somewhat expected, the well-known crypto critic Peter Schiff also chipped in. He thinks that if BTC breaks below $50K, it could collapse all the way down to the 2022 low of around $16,500. The Bottom is Here Despite the unfavorable market conditions, Altcoin Sherpa and Merlijn The Trader offered some much-needed optimism, signaling that it isn’t all doom and gloom for Bitcoin. The former claimed the current levels represent the local bottom, but the analyst remains unsure how long it will take for the asset to start a meaningful rebound. “Great entries rarely stick around for a long time, and any ideas for an immediate move seem a bit stale at this point,” they stated. The latter noted that BTC has plummeted in a similar fashion after the previous US midterm elections in 2014, 2018, and 2022, and a year after the vote it was higher every time. He predicted that a pump above $65,700 could open the door to a rise toward $95,000 and eventually $107,500. At the same time, he warned that a dip below $60K on the weekly timeframe would invalidate the scenario. title: Twenty One Capital buys 154 BTC for $10M as XXI stock slides 7.9%
body: BitcoinWorld Twenty One Capital buys 154 BTC for $10M as XXI stock slides 7.9% Tether-backed Twenty One Capital purchased 154.32 Bitcoin for roughly $10 million in cash on November 16, 2026, lifting its reported treasury to about 43,668 BTC, according to Crypto.news . The company said it paid an average of $64,801.01 per coin and financed the purchase entirely with cash. The buy followed a weekend selloff that pushed Bitcoin toward $62,000 on November 15 before the cryptocurrency recovered to trade near $65,000. Twenty One Capital acquired 154.32 Bitcoin for about $10 million on November 16, 2026, bringing its treasury to roughly 43,668 BTC. The purchase was disclosed after the market close, following a 7.88% decline in XXI shares to $4.56. Key facts Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 BTC at an average price of $64,801.01 for approximately $10 million in cash. The company’s reported treasury now stands at about 43,668 BTC, up from 43,514 BTC at September 30. XXI shares closed at $4.56 on November 16, down 7.88% from Friday’s $4.95 close, before the purchase announcement circulated. Twenty One reported third-quarter net income of $1.087 billion, driven by a $1.093 billion gain from Bitcoin fair-value accounting. The purchase was financed with cash on hand, which stood at $102.8 million as of September 30, per its SEC filing. Why the purchase followed a weekend decline CEO Rapha Zagury framed the acquisition as a decision to deploy cash at a lower Bitcoin price. “Bitcoin is our benchmark for every investment decision we make,” Zagury said in the November 16 announcement. “Any business we acquire has to beat simply buying more Bitcoin, and this weekend’s drop in price made adding Bitcoin an easy decision.” He added that every dollar spent, whether on Bitcoin, acquisitions, or buybacks, is weighed against maintaining flexibility to run the business. The purchase was the first disclosed addition to Twenty One’s Bitcoin holdings since it went public through a merger with Cantor Equity Partners in December 2025. Bitcoin Magazine reported that the buy broke a nine-month pause in treasury activity; the only change between December 2025 and September 30, 2026, was a single bitcoin transferred on March 31 as a vendor payment. The Bitcoin Magazine report also noted the company’s cost basis was about $3.69 billion at September 30, or roughly $84,900 per coin, meaning the new coins came in about $20,000 below that average while the treasury as a whole remained underwater at current prices. Twenty One’s cash position stood at $102.8 million at the end of September, down from $117.7 million at the end of 2025, according to its latest SEC filing. The $10 million purchase is equivalent to about 9.7% of that September balance. The company also carries $486.5 million of convertible notes secured by roughly 16,116 BTC pledged as collateral, which the filing says are not available for general corporate purposes while they back the debt. Shares trade below the value of the company’s Bitcoin Twenty One’s NYSE-listed stock closed November 16 at $4.56, down 7.88% from Friday’s $4.95 close. The announcement was distributed after the regular US trading session, meaning the decline preceded public disclosure of the purchase. The shares traded at $9.30 on January 2, 2026, putting their decline at roughly 51% from the first trading session of the year. Bitcoin Magazine noted that the company’s 346.65 million Class A shares outstanding at that price are worth about $1.58 billion, well below the market value of its Bitcoin holdings. That gap has been a central issue for Zagury since he replaced founder Jack Mallers as CEO in July. In an August shareholder letter, he acknowledged investor concerns about the stock trading at a discount to its Bitcoin and said Twenty One “must become more than a Bitcoin treasury.” Tether took control of the company in May after buying out SoftBank’s stake. Zagury’s November 13 shareholder letter said repurchasing shares can deserve consideration when their price is below the value of assets attributable to them, subject to liquidity and required approvals. He did not announce a buyback program. Quarterly accounting gains and a nine-month loss In its November 13 shareholder letter, Twenty One disclosed third-quarter net income of $1.087 billion, driven chiefly by a $1.093 billion gain from revaluing its Bitcoin holdings. That result was not equivalent to cash generated from operations, the company noted. Its September 30 balance sheet valued 43,514 BTC at roughly $83,700 apiece, well above Bitcoin’s November price near $65,000. Twenty One previously reported a $413.5 million second-quarter loss following a decline in Bitcoin’s value. Its nine-month financial results through September still showed a net loss of $186.5 million despite the third-quarter accounting gain. A continued decline in Bitcoin’s price would reduce the recorded value of existing coins at the next accounting date, but the company has not published fourth-quarter results. Why it matters The purchase adds a small increment to one of the largest corporate Bitcoin treasuries, but it arrives as Twenty One’s stock trades at a discount to the value of its coins — a structural problem for a company whose public market valuation is closely tied to Bitcoin’s price. The move signals that management sees price declines as buying opportunities rather than risks to the balance sheet. It also illustrates the accounting volatility inherent in a Bitcoin-heavy treasury: a single quarter can swing from a billion-dollar gain to a nine-month loss depending on the asset’s price at reporting dates. Michael Saylor, Strategy’s executive chairman, welcomed the purchase on X, writing, “Conviction doesn’t change with the price. Well done, Twenty One.” Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino shared the announcement with the message “XXI++.” The purchase landed the same day Strategy disclosed buying 485 BTC for $33.4 million, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC, as Bitcoin Magazine reported. What to watch Twenty One said further Bitcoin purchases will depend on market prices, available cash, and competing investment opportunities, without committing to a timetable or amount. The company also plans to build cash-generating businesses in mining, lending, treasury services, and energy, but has not announced a completed acquisition under that plan. Investors will be watching whether the gap between XXI’s share price and the value of its Bitcoin narrows, and whether Zagury’s strategy of acquiring profitable businesses begins to materialize. Market snapshot At the time of writing (November 17, 2026, 15:20 UTC), Bitcoin traded at $64,875 (₹6,065,324), down 12.5% over the past seven days but up 1.1% in the last 24 hours, according to CoinPaprika data. The cryptocurrency’s market capitalization stood at $1.30 trillion, with 24-hour trading volume of $21.56 billion. Frequently Asked Questions How much Bitcoin does Twenty One Capital hold now? CEO Rapha Zagury said the weekend price drop made adding Bitcoin an easy decision, as Bitcoin remains the benchmark for all investment decisions. How did XXI stock react to the purchase? XXI shares closed at $4.56 on November 16, down 7.88% from the previous close, before the purchase announcement was circulated after market hours. What was Twenty One Capital’s third-quarter profit? The company reported $1.087 billion in third-quarter net income, largely from a $1.093 billion fair-value gain on its Bitcoin holdings.
